main_dirt.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise. A unique oiled sand/dirt oval in Australian TAB racing. Features a 340m home straight. The surface generates intense kickback, creating a massive natural bias toward early front-runners ('E') and pocket pressers ('P') who can race on the lead or rail away from spray. Deep closers ('S') suffer severe kickback penalties.
main_dirt.post_bias: Inside barriers (stalls 1-4) hold a paramount advantage in 1000m, 1100m, and 1200m sprints to hold the rail into the first turn and avoid severe dirt kickback.

handicapping_angles.oiled_dirt_kickback_and_speed_bias: Fannie Bay plays like a classic US dirt track. Heavily upgrade early speed ('E') types capable of crossing and securing the fence. Severely downgrade backmarkers ('C') who dislike dirt kickback in their faces.
handicapping_angles.darwin_cup_carnival_shipper_advantage: During the July/August Darwin Cup Carnival, major interstate yards (SA, VIC, WA) send targeted runners. Interstate shippers with proven synthetic or dirt speed figures hold a major class edge over local NT form lines.
handicapping_angles.dirt_experience_filter: Always check for prior dirt, sand, or synthetic surface experience. Horses making their dirt debut from pure lush grass circuits often struggle with the kickback and firm sand footing.
handicapping_angles.nt_handicap_weight_penalty: In NT Benchmark handicaps under heavy tropical heat, top weights carrying 60kg+ face an exaggerated physical tax. Favor fit, light-weighted runners receiving apprentice claim relief.
